## Purpose

This SOP describes the use of the standard Secchi disk and the Secchi
disk tube (transparency tube) for measuring water transparency in
lakes, reservoirs, and streams. Secchi depth is one of the oldest and
simplest limnological measurements, providing a rapid estimate of the
photic zone depth and an index of suspended particle concentration
[@wetzel2001; @carlson1977].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Visual transparency measurements in lakes, ponds,
  and reservoirs (standard Secchi disk) and in streams, shallow
  wetlands, and stormwater basins (Secchi tube)
- **Does not apply to:** Quantitative turbidity measurements (see
  [SOP-F205](SOP-F205-handheld-turbidity-meter.qmd)); laboratory
  transmissometry; PAR light profiles (requires an underwater quantum
  sensor)
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Specify measurement protocol for the project            |
| Trained Personnel | Perform measurements per this SOP                       |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Euphotic zone depth ($z_{eu}$):** The depth receiving at least 1%
  of surface irradiance; approximately 2--3 times the Secchi depth in
  most lakes; defines the lower boundary of net photosynthesis
  [@wetzel2001].
- **Photic zone:** The surface layer of a water body receiving
  sufficient light to support photosynthesis; its depth is inversely
  related to turbidity and Secchi depth.
- **Secchi depth ($z_{SD}$):** The depth at which a standard Secchi
  disk becomes just invisible when lowered, averaged with the depth at
  which it becomes visible again when raised;
  $z_{SD} = (D_1 + D_2) / 2$; an index of water transparency
  inversely related to suspended particle concentration and dissolved
  color [@carlson1977].
- **Secchi tube (transparency tube):** A clear acrylic tube, typically
  60 or 120 cm long, with a Secchi disk pattern printed at the bottom
  and a drain valve at the base; filled with sample water and drained
  until the pattern disappears; used in shallow or turbid waters where
  a standard disk cannot be deployed vertically.
- **Trophic state index (TSI):** A numerical scale relating Secchi
  depth, chlorophyll a, and total phosphorus to lake trophic status;
  Carlson's TSI for Secchi depth:
  $\text{TSI}(SD) = 60 - 14.41 \ln(z_{SD})$ [@carlson1977].
- **Viewscope:** A tube, box, or bucket with a transparent bottom used
  to eliminate surface glare when reading Secchi depth; improves
  consistency between observers but must be noted and applied
  consistently within a dataset.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Secchi disk measurements from boats, docks, or bridges
  require caution to prevent falls. Wear a personal flotation device
  (PFD) when sampling from boats.
- **Biological:** Surface water may contain pathogens. Avoid ingestion;
  wear gloves if hands contact water.
- **Sun glare:** Measuring Secchi depth requires looking directly into
  the water; use polarized sunglasses or a viewscope to reduce glare
  (note use in the field notebook for consistency).
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots
- [ ] Personal flotation device (boat sampling)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (recommended for impaired waters)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunglasses)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). If
sampling from a boat, ensure all occupants know the location of PFDs
and throwable flotation devices.


## Equipment and Materials

### Standard Secchi Disk

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Standard Secchi disk (20 cm diameter) | Alternating black and white quadrants; weighted to sink horizontally |
| Graduated line (marked every 0.1 m)   | Non-stretch braided cord or chain        |
| Viewscope (optional)                  | Eliminates surface glare; a capped PVC section with a clear bottom works well |

### Secchi Tube (Transparency Tube)

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Secchi tube (60 or 120 cm)            | Clear acrylic tube; Secchi disk pattern at bottom; cm scale on side; drain valve at base |
| Sample bucket or wide-mouth bottle    | For collecting water to fill the tube    |

### General

| Item            | Notes                                              |
|:----------------|:---------------------------------------------------|
| Field notebook  | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |
| Watch           | For recording time of measurement                  |
| Camera          | For documenting site conditions                    |


## Procedure

### Standard Secchi Disk (Lakes, Reservoirs, Deep Pools)

Take measurements on the shaded side of the boat or dock, between
10:00 and 14:00 local time for consistency. Avoid measurements during
heavy cloud cover, rain, or high wind [@wetzel2001].

1. Lower the Secchi disk on the shaded side until it just disappears
   from view. Record this depth as **D1** (disappearance depth).
2. Slowly raise the disk until it just reappears. Record this depth as
   **D2** (reappearance depth).
3. Calculate Secchi depth:
   $$\text{Secchi depth} = \frac{D_1 + D_2}{2}$$
4. Record in the field notebook:
   - Secchi depth (m) and D1, D2 individually
   - Date and time
   - Sky conditions (clear, partly cloudy, overcast)
   - Wind and water surface conditions
   - Whether a viewscope was used
   - Observer name (readings vary between observers)
5. If the disk is visible on the bottom, record
   "Secchi depth > [bottom depth]" and note the bottom depth.
6. Repeat the measurement a second time; the two readings should agree
   within 0.5 m. Record both and report the mean.

### Secchi Tube (Streams, Shallow Waters)

1. Collect a water sample from mid-depth using a bucket or wide-mouth
   bottle; avoid disturbing sediment.
2. Pour the sample into the Secchi tube until full.
3. Hold the tube vertically and look down through the water column at
   the Secchi pattern on the bottom.
4. Open the drain valve slowly. Watch the Secchi pattern.
5. When the pattern just disappears, close the valve and read the
   water level on the graduated scale. Record as **Secchi tube depth**
   (cm).
6. Refill the tube and repeat; the two readings should agree within
   2 cm. Record both and report the mean.
7. Rinse the tube with DI water between sites to prevent
   cross-contamination.


## Data Interpretation

Secchi depth is inversely related to turbidity and suspended particle
concentration [@carlson1977; @wetzel2001]. Approximate trophic-state
guidelines for lakes:

| Secchi Depth (m) | Trophic Class        |
|:-----------------|:---------------------|
| > 5              | Oligotrophic         |
| 2--5             | Mesotrophic          |
| 1--2             | Eutrophic            |
| < 1              | Hypereutrophic       |

::: {.callout-note}
These categories are approximate and vary with dissolved color, algal
species, and suspended sediment type. Do not use Secchi depth alone to
classify trophic state; combine with nutrient and chlorophyll data
[@carlson1977].
:::


## Quality Control

- Use the same observer for repeated measurements at a monitoring site
  whenever possible; inter-observer variability is the largest source
  of error [@wetzel2001].
- Always take duplicate measurements and report the mean.
- Record consistently whether sunglasses or a viewscope were used.
- Verify Secchi tube graduation markings against a ruler at least once
  per year.
- When both a Secchi disk and a turbidity meter are available, pair
  the measurements to develop a site-specific Secchi-turbidity
  regression.

## Training Record

Before performing Secchi measurements independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Perform supervised duplicate Secchi disk or Secchi tube
   measurements at one site
3. Demonstrate agreement within the QC criteria (0.5 m for disk,
   2 cm for tube)
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
